reranked_evidence.title: Bond market anxiety is growing over AI capex budgets - CNBC
reranked_evidence.snippet: * Yields climbed this week after Alphabet lifted its capex forecast for its AI buildout, raising concerns that other hyperscalers would do the same. * Google, Amazon and Meta are seeing credit spreads widen as fixed-income investors demand more reward on the companies they lend to. * Oracle's 5-year credit default swap has become a go-to proxy for AI debt fears, currently trading at a multi-year high. It's playing out in real time in the bond market, where the biggest names involved in the blitz — Google, Amazon and Meta — are seeing credit spreads widen as fixed-income investors demand more reward to lend to the companies. The analysts added that the hyperscalers are currently on track to collectively spend more on capex than they generate in free cash flow by next year. Oracle is facing questions from investors about how active it plans to be in the debt market in the coming years, as the buildout and leasing of data centers continue to become more capital intensive.

reranked_evidence.title: The European city overlooked by Australian tourists - have you been? - Oberon Review
reranked_evidence.snippet: Like a lesson in humanity, it was the stronger and purer emotion that came to define the legacy of Warsaw's Old Town. Looking at the historic centre of the Polish capital city today, it's actually hard to believe that this vast area with thousands of beautiful buildings is just decades - rather than centuries - old. Because as I walk across the cobblestones of the main square, into the streets with their medieval layout and Renaissance and Baroque facades, it feels like the layers of heritage you expect from a European capital. The city centre has been meticulously recreated to look exactly how it once did. To understand the story of Warsaw's Old Town, we need to go back to the start of World War II, when the historic centre was still a marvellous collection of original buildings, including brightly coloured merchant houses, a soaring cathedral, and historic barbican walls. The buildings look exactly like they once did, even down to the windows and the colours.

reranked_evidence.snippet: Reading: OPINION: How data collaboration is helping travel advisors thrive in a crowded market. # OPINION: How data collaboration is helping travel advisors thrive in a crowded market. One of the biggest opportunities emerging across the travel industry is data collaboration. **As travellers become increasingly price-conscious, data collaboration is helping travel advisors deliver more personalised recommendations, spot changing booking trends earlier, and provide better value in an increasingly competitive market, writes Melanie Hoptman (pictured), VP and Managing Director, Brands and Agencies, APAC, LiveRamp**. The travel industry continues to be in a state of flux. One of the biggest opportunities emerging across the industry is data collaboration, which involves connecting data from various sources to generate combined insights for product development, analytics, and targeted campaigns. When first-party data is safely connected with insights from airlines, hotels, destinations, or media partners, travel advisors can identify not only where someone wants to travel but why, how, and what they value most.

reranked_evidence.title: On Thin Ice by Charlie Walker review – a Siberian adventure goes off the rails - The Guardian
reranked_evidence.snippet: # On Thin Ice by Charlie Walker review – a Siberian adventure goes off the rails. “The plan,” he writes, “was simple in concept.” A sub-zero camping trip through a region populated by wolves and bears and scarred by centuries of historical trauma, in a country that was about to invade one of its neighbours: what could possibly go wrong? On Thin Ice is Walker’s third travelogue. Reading his latest, it’s clear he’s familiar with the terrain on both sides of that line. But, reasoning that “Yakutsk is comfortably closer to the Alaskan city of Anchorage than it is to Kyiv”, he presses on. Armed with a flare gun, a can of pepper spray and a dagger for protection from the wolves and bears, Walker spends weeks trudging along ice roads – *zimniki* – by day, shivering in his tent at night, and occasionally experiencing the extremes of Siberian hospitality.

reranked_evidence.title: US on track to have historically low number of homicides in 2026, report says - Chicago Tribune
reranked_evidence.snippet: Crime and Public Safety |   US on track to have historically low number of…. # US on track to have historically low number of homicides in 2026, report says. LOS ANGELES — Data collected from 30 American cities showed an 18% decrease in the homicide rate from 2025 compared to the same period in 2026, translating to about 215 fewer homicides this year, according to a new report from the independent Council on Criminal Justice. That suggests the most significant factors contributing to the improvements are taking place nationwide and are not specific to a single local public safety measure, said Adam Gelb, the president and CEO of the Council on Criminal Justice, a nonpartisan think tank for criminal justice policy and research. Notably, Gelb said that a significant number of violent crimes were less deadly: There was a 23% drop in the lethality of the crimes committed, which is measured by the share of serious violent crime that is fatal.

reranked_evidence.title: Mamdani admin wants sweeping powers to OK new bike and bus lanes — deepening fight over NYC streets - New York Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Mamdani admin wants sweeping powers to OK new bike and bus lanes — deepening fight over NYC streets. The Mamdani administration wants to give the Department of Transportation sweeping new power to approve new bike and bus lanes, claiming it’ll speed up such projects by 33% — deepening an already bitter fight over the city’s streets. Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s office, in a press release detailing the five ballot questions, touted that the proposal would “Speed up street safety projects, including bike lanes, by at least 33%.”. New York City has more than 1,316 miles of cycling lanes, including more than 140 miles of on-street protected bike lanes, according to DOT. The agency installed 27.9 miles of new protected bike lanes in fiscal year 2025 and DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn told the City Council in early March that the agency expected to outperform that in 2026, but didn’t give a target.
